Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-defined opacity in the posterior aspect of the right hemithorax. Crucially, this mass forms an obtuse angle with the chest wall, which is a classic radiographic sign indicating an extrapulmonary origin, such as a pleural-based mass (e.g., solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura or mesothelioma), rather than a pulmonary nodule which would typically form an acute angle.
